paper_metadata.title: Multiscale chemical ordering heterogeneity facilitates exceptional strength and ductility in additively manufactured Ti-added AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high-entropy alloys at intermediate temperatures

evidence.quote: The AlCoCrFeNi ₂ . ₁ eutectic HEA (EHEA), first designed in 2014 ( Lu et al., 2015 ), is particularly notable for its superior balance of strength and ductility, stemming from the coexistence of multiple phases and eutectic microstructures

Both EHEA and EHEA-Ti specimens were fabricated via Laser Engineered Net Shaping (LENS, MR-7, Optomec) with a 2 mm laser beam in an argon environment ( < 100 ppm oxygen).
In this study, Ti powder was added to pre-alloyed AlCoCrFeNi ₂ . ₁ EHEA powder to form an AlCoCrFeNi ₂ . ₁ -Ti0.15 composition by adding 2.5 at % Ti powder (hereafter referred to as EHEA-Ti).
Both EHEA and EHEA-Ti specimens were fabricated via Laser Engineered Net Shaping (LENS, MR-7, Optomec) with a 2 mm laser beam in an argon environment ( < 100 ppm oxygen).

Samples (35 mm × 15 mm × 5 mm) were built layer-by-layer with 90° alternating scan directions and the location of the cutting samples ( Fig. 1 c), using 400 W laser power and 6 mm/s scanning speed. The laser nozzle was raised 0.3 mm after each layer.
